Question

Is drug resistance spreading between cases?

Find out whether resistant infections share a resistant strain, or acquired resistance separately.

Answering this takes two kinds of analysis: one to find resistance, and one to measure relatedness. Neither answers the question alone.

Which protocol to use

Choose the group your pathogen belongs to.

If the pathogen is Bacteria

Use these protocols together

  1. AMR gene detection and trackingPlanned protocol, not yet available

    Identify which isolates carry resistance genes or mutations.

  2. Bacterial phylogenomic surveillance

    Determine whether the resistant isolates are closely related.

If resistant isolates cluster closely, resistance is likely spreading with a single strain. If the same resistance gene appears in unrelated isolates, it may be spreading on a mobile element such as a plasmid, which needs plasmid analysis beyond these protocols.

If the pathogen is Fungi

Use these protocols together

  1. Antifungal resistance mutation detectionPlanned protocol, not yet available

    Identify which isolates carry resistance mutations.

  2. Fungal phylogenomic surveillance

    Determine whether the resistant isolates are closely related.

If resistant isolates cluster closely, a resistant strain is likely spreading. The same mutation in unrelated isolates suggests resistance arose independently, for example under drug pressure.
